findings.title: Harvard University CIO FAQ on November 2025 Alumni Affairs and Development breach
findings.summary_md: Harvard University Information Technology published an FAQ on November 22, 2025, stating that on November 18, 2025 an unauthorized party accessed Alumni Affairs and Development information systems via a phone-based phishing attack, and access was removed immediately. The breached systems do not generally contain Social Security numbers, passwords, payment card information, or financial account numbers, but do include email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, donation details, and biographical information tied to fundraising and alumni engagement. Affected groups include alumni, alumni spouses, partners, and widows or widowers, donors, parents of current and former students, and some current students, faculty, and staff. Harvard engaged third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement to investigate.

findings.title: Data Breach at Harvard's Development Office May Have Exposed Donor Records, Personal Information
findings.summary_md: The Harvard Crimson reported on November 22, 2025 that Harvard's Alumni Affairs and Development Office systems were accessed by an unauthorized party earlier that week after a phone-based phishing attack, discovered November 18, 2025. CIO Klara Jelinkova and Alumni Affairs and Development chief James J. Husson wrote that accessed systems include donation details and event attendance records plus email addresses, telephone numbers, and home addresses, and do not generally contain Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial account numbers. Harvard had not yet decided whether to send specific notifications to affected affiliates and was working with third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement. The article noted similar donor and alumni record breaches at Princeton University earlier that month and at the University of Pennsylvania in October.

findings.title: Harvard University discloses data breach affecting alumni, donors
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on November 24, 2025 that Harvard disclosed a breach of Alumni Affairs and Development systems caused by a phone-based phishing (vishing) attack discovered November 18, 2025. The article echoed Harvard's statement that the accessed systems do not generally contain Social Security numbers, passwords, payment card information, or financial account numbers. Harvard engaged third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement and launched a webpage with updates and an FAQ.

findings.title: Harvard reports vishing breach exposing alumni and donor contact data
findings.summary_md: SecurityAffairs reported on November 24, 2025 that Harvard revealed its Alumni Affairs and Development systems suffered a vishing breach exposing contact, donation, and biographical data of students, staff, and alumni, with no Social Security numbers, passwords, payment card data, or financial information stored in the breached systems. Harvard officials believe the breach exposed information belonging to alumni, their spouses, partners, and widows or widowers, donors, parents of current and former students, and some current students, faculty, and staff. The university launched an investigation with external cybersecurity experts, notified law enforcement, and sent data breach notifications to affected individuals on November 22, 2025.

findings.title: Harvard Alumni Affairs Databases Breached
findings.summary_md: Harvard Magazine reported on November 25, 2025 that Harvard officials said the breach was discovered November 18, 2025 and that the university acted immediately to remove the attacker's access, with no evidence of further unauthorized access. The accessed systems do not generally contain Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial account numbers, but include personal information such as email addresses, telephone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, details of donations, and biographical information pertaining to fundraising and alumni engagement. Harvard notified affected individuals and launched an investigation with third-party cybersecurity experts and law enforcement.

findings.title: Hackers publish personal information stolen during Harvard, UPenn data breaches
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported on February 4, 2026 that ShinyHunters published what it claims are more than one million records from Harvard and UPenn on its leak site after the universities refused to pay a ransom. TechCrunch verified a portion of the dataset by matching records against alumni and public records such as student ID numbers, and reported the published data appears to match the types Harvard disclosed as stolen: email addresses, phone numbers, home and business addresses, event attendance, donation details, and biographical information. The hackers told TechCrunch the intrusions were part of a recently disclosed phishing campaign targeting Okta and single sign-on providers, and Harvard did not respond to a request for comment.

findings.title: A Technical and Ethical Post-Mortem of the Feb 2026 Harvard University ShinyHunters Data Breach
findings.summary_md: InfoStealers published on February 4, 2026 an analysis stating ShinyHunters, operating as part of the Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters collective, exposed approximately 115,000 sensitive records from Harvard's Alumni Affairs and Development department. The post describes the likely attack vector as vishing and SSO bypass consistent with the group's modus operandi, and notes the leak exposed stewardship and donor-related data. It frames the incident as a collapse of institutional data sovereignty affecting Harvard's donor base.

findings.title: Massive data leak hits Harvard and UPenn
findings.summary_md: CyberNews reported on February 5, 2026 that ShinyHunters dumped data stolen from Harvard and UPenn after ransom refusal, and that Harvard discovered the breach on November 18, 2025 following a phone-based phishing attack. The coverage noted ShinyHunters claimed more than one million records per university and that the leaked data includes alumni donor information, contact details, and fundraising records. CyberNews contextualized the incident within a wave of social-engineering attacks against university alumni and donor systems.
